mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-command-execution
mechanisms.what: `E2BSubprocessHandle` projects one E2B background command onto the `SubprocessHandle` seam. Its constructor returns synchronously while `run()` resolves the shared sandbox, calls `prepareState`, then `sandbox.commands.run(commandText(spec, paths), {background: true, cwd, envs: e2bControlEnvs(controlEnvs), stdin: …, timeoutMs: 0, onStdout, onStderr})`. `commandText` emits a two-stage bash wrapper: a bootstrap that resolves `env`/`setsid`/`bash`/`node`/`ps`/`tr`/`tee`/`head`/`rm` with `command -v` and refuses unless every one is an absolute executable (`exit 125`), then `exec env -i -- "${dsh_e2b_env[@]}" setsid --wait -- bash -c <inner> … <argv>`; the inner script writes its own PGID to `<stateDir>/pid`, reads the NUL-delimited environment file, removes it, runs the target under `env -i`, writes the exit status to `<stateDir>/exit-code`, then `wait`s and exits with that status.
invariants: Each handle starts through the shared sandbox and retains command output/status paths in that remote world. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:2-3)

The bootstrap ends in an exec chain through the scrubbed environment and `setsid`, so E2B's command PID is the provisional group id even before the private publication file can be trusted. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:571-574)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — spawn-time validation throws synchronously (disposing service, empty argv[0], unrepresentable grace, pre-aborted signal, NUL bytes); runtime failures roll back through `rollbackPublishedFailure`/`removeFailedState` and reject `done`; a cancellation during preparation resolves as `{exitCode: null, signal: 'SIGTERM'}` rather than throwing (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:383).

constants.meaning: default `pollMs` — remote status/liveness poll cadence; each tick is one control-plane request
bootstrap refusal when any required tool is not an absolute executable
no SDK-side command timeout; deadlines stay with the caller
per-spawn private remote state directory
private mode on the state directory and its files

mechanisms.name: e2b-base64-output-transport
mechanisms.what: Remote stdout/stderr travel as newline-delimited base64 frames produced by `OUTPUT_ENCODER_SOURCE`, a Node one-liner piped to `node -e` inside the wrapper (with `head -c <maxSpillBytes>` and `tee` writing the private spill file first when the mode has a spill). `E2BBase64Decoder.push(text)` buffers arbitrarily split SDK callbacks, splits on `\n`, rejects a frame that is not valid base64 or that does not round-trip (`bytes.toString('base64') !== frame`), recognizes the reserved `E2B_OUTPUT_COMPLETE_FRAME` as clean EOF, and throws on a duplicate completion or on any frame after completion. `finish(requireComplete)` throws `truncated base64 output transport` when a partial frame remains and `incomplete output transport` when the EOF frame never arrived; a requested termination passes `requireComplete = false` to discard the interrupted tail.
invariants: Decode every complete newline-delimited frame in one arbitrarily split SDK callback. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/output.ts:17)
Reserved non-base64 frame proving that one remote encoder reached clean EOF. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/output.ts:8)
the round-trip re-encode check `bytes.toString('base64') !== frame` is the acceptance test for a frame (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/output.ts:40-42)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a transport fault is recorded in `outputTransportError`, the corresponding host stream is destroyed with it, and `run()` rethrows it after the command settles; the decoders' `finish()` rejects an incomplete transport instead of returning partial data as complete.

constants.meaning: E2B_OUTPUT_COMPLETE_FRAME, the reserved EOF frame
BASE64_TEXT pre-check before the round-trip verification
when a clean EOF frame is demanded

mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-environment-resolution
mechanisms.what: `readRemoteEnvironment(sandbox)` runs one control command that resolves the login user's home from `getent passwd` and then prints the home and `env -0` output **as base64** (`base64 -w 0`) so SDK callback chunking cannot corrupt UTF-8; it validates exactly two base64 lines, decodes with a fatal UTF-8 `TextDecoder`, requires an absolute NUL-free home, forces `HOME` to that value, and returns a NUL-delimited string. `scrubRemoteEnvironment` drops every `DSH_*` name and anything matching `SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN`; `bootstrapEnvironment` returns `{TERM: 'dumb'}` plus an empty-string override for each private/credential-shaped name (so the bootstrap login shell does not see them); `serializeRemoteEnvironment` overlays explicit caller entries, where an explicit `undefined` is the seam's tombstone that deletes an ambient entry, and rejects names that are empty/contain `=`/NUL or values containing NUL.
invariants: Read the remote environment through ASCII base64 so SDK callback chunking cannot corrupt UTF-8. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/environment.ts:23)

TODO(e2b-replace-environment): Remove this ambient probe when E2B can start a command with a replacement environment instead of merged overrides. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/environment.ts:29-30)
Isolate E2B's fixed login-shell bootstrap from user profiles and ambient credentials. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/environment.ts:72)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — invalid base64, non-UTF-8 bytes, an invalid home, or an invalid explicit entry all throw; the environment file is deleted remotely right after the wrapper reads it (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:114).

constants.meaning: the single ambient probe command
the only entry bootstrapEnvironment always sets
shared credential-shaped name filter used for the remote scrub too

mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-process-group-quiescence
mechanisms.what: Termination and quiescence are proved with control-plane probes keyed on a numeric PGID. `groupAlive` runs `ps -eo pgid=,stat= | awk '$1 == <pid> && $2 !~ /^[ZXx]/ { live=1 } END { if (live) print "live" }'` and treats `SandboxNotFoundError` as 'not alive'. `terminate()` aborts the internal `terminationController`, destroys the host pipes and starts `terminateRemote()` once; `terminateGroup` sends `TERM` to the group, waits for group exit within `spec.graceMs`, and on failure escalates to `SIGKILL` via `forceKillGroup` (group `kill -KILL` **and** `handle.kill()`), then requires `waitForGroupExit` to prove emptiness or throws `remote process group <id> remained live after force termination`. `waitForExit(signal)` blocks until the group is gone. `signalRemoteGroups` is the single tolerant signal path: it swallows `CommandExitError` (groups already gone) and `SandboxNotFoundError`.
invariants: A same-UID sandbox process can rewrite this file; refuse ids whose negative form addresses every process (`kill -- -1`) or init's group. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:493-495)
the final liveness probe, not either transport's self-report, proves cleanup (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:632)

TODO(e2b-pgid-identity): Prefer an atomic identity-bound group signal if E2B adds one; a userspace identity precheck cannot close the numeric-PGID reuse race. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/remote.ts:87-88)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a group that survives the KILL round throws; a recorded `terminationFailure` is rethrown from `waitForExit`; only `SandboxNotFoundError` is treated as proof of quiescence.

constants.meaning: published PGID must be a positive safe integer greater than 1

constants.value: exitCode > 255 rejected, raw status must match /^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/
constants.meaning: acceptance test on the published exit-code file
group signal form used by both ladders
waitForGroupExit deadline = Date.now() + spec.graceMs

mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-pty-terminal
mechanisms.what: `spawnE2BTerminal` writes a private state directory (0700) holding `runner.bash` (`TERMINAL_RUNNER_SOURCE`), the NUL-delimited `environment` and `argv` files and a random `output-marker` (all 0600), allocates the PTY with `sandbox.pty.create({rows, cols, cwd, envs, timeoutMs: 0, onData})`, then types `exec /bin/bash <runner> <stateDir>\r` into it. The runner prints the marker and then `exec env -i -- "${dsh_env[@]}" "${dsh_argv[@]}"`, so the bootstrap login shell is replaced by the requested argv; `BootstrapOutputFilter` withholds all host output until the marker appears and then forwards only what follows it, and `waitForBootstrapOutput` bounds that with the caller signal and the command completion. Afterwards `terminalSessionId` resolves the POSIX session via `ps -o sid= -p <pid>` and an `E2BTerminalHandle` is returned.
invariants: Allocate an E2B PTY, replace its bootstrap shell with the requested argv, and return only after the private runner has published readiness. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:449-452)
terminal runner received empty argv -> exit 125 (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:38-41)
the retained bytes are at most marker.length - 1 so a split marker can still be matched on the next chunk (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:76-77)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — every setup step is inside one try; the catch destroys the output stream and runs a `cleanup` that kills/rolls back the terminal (`rollbackUnpublishedTerminal`) and removes the state directory, aggregating any failure into `AggregateError` before rethrowing the original error.

constants.meaning: the per-spawn output marker the filter waits for
runner refusal on empty argv
private mode on the terminal state directory and its four files
no SDK-side PTY timeout
per-terminal private remote state directory

mechanisms.name: e2b-terminal-session-scoping
mechanisms.what: An E2B terminal is owned at the whole POSIX session level rather than one PGID: `terminalSessionId` resolves the session with `ps -o sid= -p <pid>` and `sessionProcessGroups` lists every live group in that session with `ps -eo sid=,pgid=,stat= | awk '$1 == <sid> && $3 !~ /^[ZXx]/ { print $2 }'`, rejecting any group <= 1. `E2BTerminalHandle.signalForeground` resolves the foreground group with `ps -o tpgid= -p <pid>` (always reporting `inputWaiting: false` because 'E2B exposes process-table commands but not the /proc memory access needed to prove a specific syscall is waiting on fd 0'), refuses to `SIGKILL` the shell itself, and sends `kill -<SIG> -- -<pgid>`. `closeOnce` walks the ladder: list groups, `TERM` + wait within grace, otherwise `SIGKILL` plus `handle.kill()` and a final kill-mode wait, then throws naming surviving groups or the surviving pid.
invariants: refusing to SIGKILL the terminal shell; terminate the terminal session instead (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:326)
E2B exposes process-table commands but not the /proc memory access needed to prove a specific syscall is waiting on fd 0. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:361-363)

TODO(e2b-pgid-identity): Replace retained numeric PTY/session ids when E2B exposes identity-bound input, foreground-signal, and cleanup operations. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/terminal.ts:303-304)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a surviving group or a live top-level pid throws; `SandboxNotFoundError` is the only accepted disappearance during cleanup; `terminate()` is idempotent (memoized promise, cleared on failure).

constants.meaning: session-id resolution command
live-group enumeration for one session
unsafe process group guard
session liveness poll cadence bounded by the grace deadline

mechanisms.name: e2b-executable-resolution
mechanisms.what: `E2BSubprocessRuntime.resolveExecutable` requires a non-empty command; for an absolute posix path it runs `test -f <cmd> -a -x <cmd>` inside the sandbox and returns the path; a bare name containing `/` is rejected as a relative path; otherwise it runs `PATH=<quoted> command -v -- <cmd>` (cwd = the shared E2B cwd, env = `env?.PATH` prefix) and requires the printed answer to be a single line that is either absolute or contains `/`, resolving a relative answer against `ctx.e2b.cwd`. Unlike subprocess-local there is no PATHEXT handling — the remote world is POSIX.
invariants: use an absolute path or a bare PATH name (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:129)
A relative result comes from a relative PATH entry; the lookup ran with the shared cwd. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:143)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — the `test` command's non-zero exit propagates as a `CommandExitError`; a multi-line or purely relative `command -v` answer throws `did not resolve to one absolute path`.

constants.meaning: absolute-path verification command
bare-name lookup command

mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-spill-and-tail-capture
mechanisms.what: `E2BOutputReader` mirrors the local collector's tail-keep semantics over a remote file: `push(bytes)` appends and trims head chunks (or `subarray`s the over-cap head) until `retainedBytes <= maxBytes`, and `readFrom(fromByte)` reports `lossy` when the requested offset precedes `totalBytes - retainedBytes`, returning the whole retained tail in that case. The `spillPath` is advertised only when the read is lossy AND the spill was not invalidated AND `maxSpillBytes` is defined AND `totalBytes <= maxSpillBytes`. `finalizeSpills` removes the remote spill file when the output-drain grace expired, when the stream did not exceed the in-memory cap, or when it exceeded the spill cap — i.e. exactly when the file can no longer hold the complete stream.
invariants: Stop advertising a remote spill whose writer did not reach clean EOF. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/output.ts:88)
The command outcome is authoritative; owner teardown bounds private residue. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:671)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — overflow and expiry set flags and drop the spill reference; a failed remote removal is swallowed so the command outcome stays authoritative; `invalidateSpill()` is called on a grace-expired drain (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:528-529).

constants.meaning: the exact condition under which the remote spill file is deleted
the remote spill write is itself byte-capped by head
grace bound on draining inherited output before the wrapper's status file is accepted

mechanisms.name: e2b-service-teardown
mechanisms.what: `E2BSubprocessRuntime`'s constructor installs `ctx.effect` teardown: it sets `disposing = true` (so later `spawn`/`spawnTerminal` throw), aborts every in-flight `TerminalSetup` controller with `subprocess-e2b: service disposed during terminal setup` and awaits their `done` promises, then for every live handle calls `terminate()` and awaits BOTH `handle.waitForExit()` and `handle.done` before deleting it from `live`, and for every terminal awaits `terminal.terminate()`. Failures are collected with `Promise.allSettled` and rethrown as one error or `AggregateError(failures, 'subprocess-e2b: teardown failed')`. Allocation is deliberately non-blocking for `spawn` (the constructor starts `run()` and returns), so `spawnTerminal` re-checks `this.disposing` after the await and terminates a terminal that lost the race.
invariants: Each handle starts through the shared sandbox and retains command output/status paths in that remote world. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:2-3)
Retain the handle so service disposal can retry its cleanup transaction. (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:181)
if this.disposing, terminate the just-allocated terminal and throw 'service disposed during terminal setup' (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:211-215)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — disposal awaits real remote quiescence per handle/terminal and rethrows single or aggregated failures; allocation after disposal has begun throws immediately.

constants.value: pollMs must be a positive safe integer
constants.meaning: constructor validation of the only config field
AggregateError message when more than one target failed

e2b/subprocess-e2b.note: Real logic, not mere plumbing: `E2BSubprocessRuntime` is a full provider of `ctx.subprocess` with its own disposal policy, remote executable resolution, synchronous-spawn/asynchronous-start projection, and private remote state management (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:60-229). `process.ts` (693 lines) is the remote ordinary-process mechanism; `terminal.ts` (567 lines) is the remote PTY mechanism; `environment.ts`/`output.ts`/`remote.ts` are the shared remote transports. Mechanisms: e2b-remote-command-execution, e2b-base64-output-transport, e2b-remote-environment-resolution, e2b-remote-process-group-quiescence, e2b-remote-pty-terminal, e2b-terminal-session-scoping, e2b-executable-resolution, e2b-remote-spill-and-tail-capture, e2b-service-teardown.

notes: All 6 .ts files read in full. Facts to carry: (1) This package is the remote twin of `subprocess-local` and shares only the seam types and `SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN`; there is no Win32/Job, no /proc inspection, and no identity fencing — quiescence is proven by re-running `ps` in the sandbox (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:651-661, terminal.ts:146-174). (2) Process-group identity is a numeric PGID read from a file that a same-UID sandbox process could rewrite; the code guards only against ids <= 1 and documents the residual reuse race in a TODO (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:493-498, remote.ts:87-88). (3) `E2BSubprocessHandle.spawn` is synchronous by contract while the remote command starts asynchronously, hence the `commandState`/`readyState` resolver pair and `DeferredStdin` (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:51-69, :166-167). (4) Unlike subprocess-local, this provider has no 'fallback' containment tier: every ordinary spawn and terminal is always group/session-contained. (5) The `exit 125` sentinel appears twice (bootstrap tool check and the terminal runner's empty-argv check) and is not translated into a Node error code.
